solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: In a sense the doctor was sent back as redundant

indicators.note: the doctor sits in the sense, so the sense word is opened up to hold him

parts.note: touch is one of the five senses

indicators.note: sent back tells us the doctor's letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor finds himself sent home because he is no longer needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns the doctor's letters around, and 'In' places them inside the sense; 'was' and 'as' are just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something superfluous is more than is needed, an excess; the phrase is a straight synonym.

clue.text: One may take it to avoid it

definitions.text: One may take it to avoid it

parts.words: One may take it to avoid it
parts.note: to take pains or care is to go to some effort, and that effort can stop difficulties arising later

explanation.surface: A paradox: you accept the very thing you are trying to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word fills both gaps: 'take ___' means make an effort, while the second 'it' means problems, which the effort averts.
explanation.definitionFit: Both 'it's are the same noun for difficulty or bother, used in the idiom about taking pains.

clue.text: Be more than an issue after being made public

indicators.note: after places the issue word behind the word for being made public

parts.note: a secret that is out has been made public
an issue of a magazine is a number

explanation.surface: Something exceeds a single magazine edition once it has been published.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed others in count is to be greater than them in quantity; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Exhaust advice on employment of umbrellas

definitions.meaning: to consume entirely, leaving none
the instruction for an umbrella is to open it and hold it aloft: employ it, raised

explanation.surface: A tip on how to use umbrellas so you do not tire yourself out.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: 'use' (employ) plus 'up' (where an umbrella goes).
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete a supply is to consume it all, the phrasal verb's ordinary meaning.

clue.text: Was indecisive, because the date is wrong

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are in the wrong order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dithered because they had the wrong date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges THE DATE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pausing out of uncertainty before acting is wavering, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Sailors' smokes

definitions.meaning: a reefer is a sailor who takes in sail, and also a sailor's short thick jacket
cannabis cigarettes, joints

explanation.walkthrough: One word, two senses: sailors who reef sails (or their jackets) and marijuana cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand-rolled joints have this slang name, while sailors' jackets and midshipmen share the same word.

clue.text: Come again about a dog

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: An order to a dog to circle round and return.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens again and again repeats itself; a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Brand associated with Arthur

parts.note: a brand is an old poetic word for a sword, and King Arthur's sword is the famous one of legend

explanation.surface: It reads like a product line named after someone called Arthur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand' suggests a trade name, but it is the archaic word for a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's legendary sword, given by the Lady of the Lake, bears this name.

clue.text: Wood sculpted by one

indicators.note: sculpted means shaped and worked, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A piece of timber carved by a single craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sculpted' rearranges BY ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard black timber from tropical trees is a type of wood, an example.

clue.text: Fields of activity of all round significance

definitions.meaning: areas of interest or influence
globes are round in every direction, so the word is all round in a literal sense

explanation.walkthrough: 'all round significance' sounds like broad importance, but it means round on all sides, as balls are.
explanation.definitionFit: Domains of influence or interest are called by this word, and a ball shape is round everywhere.

clue.text: Extravagant version of true love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: a version of a word here is a rearranged form of its letters

explanation.surface: An over-the-top take on true love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' signals the rearrangement of 'true'; 'love' is tennis's zero, placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: A borrowed French word for something eccentric, beyond the usual bounds; a synonym.

clue.text: Penitent habit of clergy after dismissal

indicators.note: after places the clergy word behind the dismissal word

parts.note: getting the sack is being dismissed from a job
the cloth is the clergy collectively

explanation.surface: A defrocked priest might take up a penitent's garb after being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' means clothing, as in a monk's habit, not a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse fabric worn as a sign of repentance, in the phrase sackcloth and ashes.

clue.text: Boy looking sad, an indication of imminent departure

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
Peter is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad looking glum because someone is about to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue flag with a white square, hoisted on a ship to signal it is about to sail.

clue.text: Course for one in egg production

definitions.meaning: a course is a row of bricks or stones in a wall
a hen that lays eggs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' is a builder's term for one row of bricks, not a meal or class.
explanation.definitionFit: A single level of material in a wall, and a hen kept for eggs, share this word.

clue.text: Drinking bender

parts.note: a bender looks like a drinking spree, but it is the joint that bends when raising a glass, as in bending the arm

explanation.surface: A heavy session in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bender' looks like a binge; it is the arm joint that bends as you lift a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm's hinge joint flexes to raise a glass, hence 'bending' it for a drink.

clue.text: European lobby in British government?

parts.note: white is used loosely for people of European descent
a hall is an entrance lobby

explanation.surface: A question of whether there is a European lobby group inside the British government.
explanation.definitionFit: The London street housing ministries stands by metonymy for the British civil service and government.

clue.text: They come to terms with cakes and sweets

definitions.text: They come to terms with cakes and sweets

parts.words: They come to terms with cakes and sweets
parts.note: at boarding school, pupils bring boxes of goodies (tuck) back each school term

explanation.surface: People reaching an agreement while eating confectionery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come to terms' sounds like reaching a deal; it means arriving for school terms. Tuck is British school slang for snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Boarding-school pupils' boxes of snacks travel with them at the start of each school term.

clue.text: Solicits votes for an artist's works

definitions.meaning: goes round seeking support in an election
paintings, which are made on canvas

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense (seeks votes) and the plural noun (paintings) share one spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Campaigners seeking support door to door do this, and oil paintings are named after their fabric.

clue.text: Oxyphenol derivative that is used by wood tappers

indicators.note: a chemical derivative is made from another compound, so the letters of the chemical name are reworked

explanation.surface: A chemical compound derived from something and used by woodworkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derivative' rearranges OXYPHENOL. 'wood tappers' sounds like woodpeckers but means players striking wooden bars.
explanation.definitionFit: This percussion instrument has wooden bars struck with mallets, so its players tap wood.

clue.text: Not allowed in Bedford after work

indicators.note: after being worked over, the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Something banned in the town of Bedford once the working day is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after work' rearranges IN BEDFORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Prohibited and banned mean the same; a straight adjective synonym.

clue.text: Got key cut

parts.note: F is a musical key
etched means cut into a surface

explanation.surface: Someone had a key cut at the locksmith.
explanation.definitionFit: To go and bring something back is to get it; a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Posh vehicle for baker's deliveries?

definitions.meaning: short for a ...-Royce, the luxury car
bread buns a baker delivers

explanation.walkthrough: The luxury car's short name and the baker's buns share one word; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rolls-Royce is known by its short name, and small bread loaves also bear that name.

clue.text: Paid as agreed

definitions.meaning: a bill ... has been paid
a matter ... has been agreed

explanation.definitionFit: A debt is cleared when paid off, and a dispute is resolved when terms are agreed.

clue.text: Record start of the event

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a race is a sporting event

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to log the beginning of a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is a line recorded by an instrument, such as a chart or graph trace.

clue.text: In the bay, wrecked ship sunk deep

indicators.note: wrecked means smashed up, so the word's letters are broken and rearranged

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A ship wrecked in the bay has sunk to the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges BAY into ABY. 'deep' is the noun, the depths, as in 'the deep'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottomless chasm or the ocean depths; the deep is a poetic name for the sea's depths.

clue.text: Dangerous situation that frightened a buccaneer to death

definitions.meaning: an accident ... is a dangerous place on a road

definitions.text: that frightened a buccaneer to death
definitions.meaning: in Treasure Island, Billy Bones receives a pirate's death summons, a black mark on paper, and dies

explanation.walkthrough: In Stevenson's Treasure Island, pirates hand a marked paper to someone condemned; Billy Bones dies of a stroke after receiving one.
explanation.definitionFit: A notorious hazard site is so called, and it is the pirates' doom token in Treasure Island.

clue.text: Muscular like some bully?

definitions.meaning: brawny and strong
bully beef is tinned corned beef, so some bully is made of beef

explanation.walkthrough: 'bully' looks like a thug, but bully beef is tinned corned beef, a British military ration.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawny build is described so, and corned meat in a tin is beef-like.

clue.text: Rising United Kingdom party's prestige

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom
a do is a party, and the 's adds an S, as in do's

explanation.surface: A political party gaining esteem across Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns UK into KU in this down clue; 'party's' supplies DO plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek-derived word for glory or renown, meaning the same as status or honour.

clue.text: Knockout blows for farm workers?

definitions.meaning: big swinging punches in boxing
people who make hay at harvest

explanation.walkthrough: A boxer's wild swinging punch and a hay-making farmhand share the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild swinging punches are named after the mowing motion, and hay harvesters are literally so called.

clue.text: Funny to see a number walk like sailors

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals
sailors roll from side to side as they walk

explanation.surface: It is comic to watch a crowd walking with a sailor's gait.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry, quirky humour is described as amusing in this way; an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Number I spread out for show

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals
to splay is to spread out, like fingers

explanation.surface: A performer splays a numbered card for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibition put on for viewing is a show; a noun synonym.

clue.text: We object during pay out to hold up

indicators.note: during puts one piece in the middle of the other, so the pay word holds the other

parts.note: to spend is to pay out money
US is the object form of the pronoun we

explanation.surface: Staff object to having their pay delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a protest verb but is grammar: US is what 'we' becomes as an object.
explanation.definitionFit: To delay or halt something temporarily, as a payment or a meeting, is to defer it.
